problems.title: The weak Euler integration chain discards nonzero hole pressure and inner boundary flux
problems.original_claim_type: paraphrase with exact source-defined formulas retained
source_locations: Weak-solution test class and pressure definition, p. 33
First display on p. 34, concluding the proof of Theorem 1.3
problems.claim: For every compactly supported smooth vector test w, the global stress integral equals its annular restriction, which equals the negative local Euler-residual integral and hence zero.
hypotheses_checked: Constructed smooth annular domain Ω and bounded hole Ω′
u solves Δu + μu = 0, with μ > 0
u|Γ_j = c_j and ∇u = 0 on both boundary components
v is the rotated gradient of u in Ω and is zero outside Ω
p = 0 outside the filled domain; p is the local Bernoulli pressure in Ω; p_h = −μ(c_2² − c_1²)/2 in the hole
All C_c∞ vector tests are permitted, not only divergence-free tests
c_2² > c_1² follows from the radial energy identity and the branch boundary values
problems.input_witness: Choose a compactly supported smooth vector field w equal to x in a neighborhood of the closure of Ω′ and zero near the outer boundary Γ_1. Such a cutoff exists because the two compact boundary components have positive separation.
problems.correct_calculation: ∫_{Ω′} div w = 2|Ω′|. Opposite normal orientations give ∫_{Γ_2} w·ν_Ω = −2|Ω′|. The interior Euler residual, kinetic boundary flux and outer pressure are zero, whereas the inner pressure p_h is nonzero. Therefore I_Ω(w) = −2p_h|Ω′| ≠ 0, while I_{Ω′}(w) = +2p_h|Ω′|. The true global integral is zero by cancellation.
problems.discrepancy: Both individual equalities in the printed global→annulus→interior-only chain fail. This is not a counterexample to the constructed global weak solution.

statements: The annular and hole fluxes sum exactly to zero

dependency_chain: False displayed reduction of the global weak integral
Theorem 1.3: stationary Euler application on the whole plane
problems.impact: A demonstrated invalid derivation directly supports a named core application in the title, abstract and Theorem 1.3. The severity concerns that derivation, not falsity of the theorem.
counterevidence: The pressure is defined correctly on the hole.
Exact interface cancellation restores the global weak equation.
Both p and the products v_i v_j are globally C¹ because ∇u vanishes at the interfaces. Direct integration by parts of the global stress also proves the weak Euler equation.
No additional existence hypothesis or new numerical experiment is needed for the repair.
alternative_readings_rejected: Restricting w to divergence-free tests changes the explicit quantifier on p. 33.
Treating Ω as the filled domain contradicts the separate domain Ω′ and the pressure definition.

repair.proposal: Retain p_h∫_{Ω′} div w and the inner pressure flux, then cancel the opposite normal contributions. Alternatively, integrate the globally C¹ stress over the whole plane.
repair.verified: Complete exact repair for every admissible vector test; no parameter restriction added.
repair.author_adoption: The assigned v2 pressure definition supplies the needed term, but the printed integration chain still omits it. No later correction was verified.
repair.remaining: Correct the displayed proof; independent acceptance and publisher-version comparison remain.

problems.title: The infinite-spectrum rigidity proof replaces inverse-square-root curvature weights by raw curvatures
source_locations: Definition of V and relation (6.11), p. 40
problems.claim: Equation (6.10) can be rewritten with the same normalized coefficients as A_r·V(s) = o(1), where V_l = k/(1 + C_l k), and then implies curvature constancy.
hypotheses_of_local_step: Distinct real constants C_l, with C_1 = 0
k(s) is nonzero on a regular interval
The coefficient vector has a fixed nonzero norm; a normalized real or imaginary part and a convergent subsequence are available
problems.actual_vector: W_l(k) = |k/(1 + C_l k)|^(−1/2), whereas V_l(k) = k/(1 + C_l k).
problems.decisive_evidence: For m = 2, k = 1, C_1 = 0, C_2 = 3 and A = (2,−1)/√5, one has W = (1,2), V = (1,1/4), A·W = 0 and A·V = 7/(4√5) ≠ 0. Thus the claimed rewriting is not a linear-algebra identity.
problems.witness_scope: Exact algebraic witness against the printed transformation at regular values. No domain/eigenfunction realization is claimed, and this is not a counterexample to Theorem 6.1.
dependency_chain: False replacement of W by V
Circular boundary and disk/annulus conclusion in Theorem 6.1
problems.impact: The invalid transformation supplies the decisive curvature step in an advertised rigidity contribution. It does not enter the main large-l construction.
counterevidence: The preceding stationary-phase formulas contain the correct inverse-square-root weights.
The corrected W weights are linearly independent by an explicit Wronskian/Vandermonde calculation.

An argument using fixed imaginary shifts supports the stationary-phase grouping and a single common coefficient subsequence, without certifying the unavailable exact large-t formulation attributed to Berenstein.

repair.proposal: Retain W, multiply the limiting relation by √|k|, and prove linear independence of f_l(k) = √|1 + C_l k|.
repair.verified: On each interval with fixed signs, f_l^(j)(k_0) = f_l(k_0) (1/2)_{falling,j} [C_l/(1 + C_l k_0)]^j. Its Wronskian is a product of nonzero factors and the Vandermonde determinant in the distinct numbers q_l = C_l/(1 + C_l k_0). A nonconstant k would therefore force A = 0, contradicting ||A|| = 1. The argument includes C_1 = 0 and negative branches of the linear factors.
repair.author_adoption: The correct weights already appear in (6.10), but the printed V remains inconsistent. No later correction was verified.
repair.remaining: Amend V and supply the linear-independence argument; retain the stated limits on external stationary-phase and nodal dependencies.

independent_acceptance_review.summary: Both reported invalid derivations are confirmed. The defined pressure has a nonzero hole value whose omitted flux cancels the annular boundary term, restoring the weak Euler result. Equation6.10 cannot be rewritten with the raw-curvature vector, but the correctly weighted functions have a nonzero Wronskian. Major grades are supported by the direct advertised theorem dependencies; neither is a counterexample to a repaired theorem or the main large-angular-mode construction.

problem_checks.assumptions: Source permits every compactly supported smooth vector test, not only divergence-free ones. The constructed annular branch hasmu>0,grad u=0onboth boundaries and unequal squared boundary values.
problem_checks.independent_derivation: E'=[(psi')^2/2+mu psi^2/2]'=-(psi')^2/r givesc2^2>c1^2 andp_h<0. Forw=xnear the closed hole and0nearouterboundary, integral_hole divw=2area andinner outward flux forannulus=-2area. LocalEuler residual is-(Delta u+mu u)grad u=0. ThereforeI_annulus=-2p_h area!=0 whileI_hole=2p_h area, so both printed intermediate equalities fail and the correct global integral vanishes.

The invalid displayed step directly proves the titled Euler application; no bifurcation/Pompeiu counterexample follows.
